# About the notes

I’m Bobby, and I teach mathematics at New York City College of Technology. I like to start with a question that a picture or a small experiment can help us answer.
:::

:::: {.lesson-prose}
The linear algebra notes begin with a circle and a slider. Before writing down the matrix, try to predict what will happen to a point on the circle. The two columns of the matrix then have a job you can see.

In probability, the question starts with two dice. Counting every possible roll gives an exact answer. Running the experiment in R shows what that answer looks like in a finite sample.
